Lua addon system (MoonSharp)¶

Player-facing docs: the authoring guide (how to write/install addons,
callbacks, the sandbox, and the migration notes for existing addons) and the
API reference (every Shroud* function). This page is the host-internals doc.

The client hosts player-written Lua addons via MoonSharp (vendored C# source,
UnityProject/Assets/Plugins/MoonSharp/). This page covers the host wiring, the
garbage-collection / frame-timing API added for tracker #914, and the current-target
API added for tracker #746.

Host wiring¶

Host: UnityProject/Assets/Scripts/Lua/LuaManager.cs (MonoBehaviour).

One shared MoonSharp.Interpreter.Script (m_bootScript, CoreModules.Preset_Complete) holds
  every enabled addon; addons are *.lua files in the user data Lua/ folder.

Only enabled addons execute. A disabled addon's body is never run into m_bootScript at load
  (ForceReload / LoadPackagedScript gate the DoString on the pref-derived enabled state, #1137),
  so a disabled addon is fully inert and contributes no globals — nothing it defines is reachable
  (including via /lua <function>) until it is enabled. Enabling runs the body: EnableScript for a
  flat addon, ForceReload for a package. The addon still gets a ScriptEntry while disabled so it
  lists in the manager.

Callbacks (ShroudOnUpdate, ShroudOnGUI, ShroudOnStart, mouse/scene/sound hooks, …) are
  detected by re-running each file in a throwaway Script and stored per addon (ScriptEntry);
  LuaManager.Update() drives ShroudOnUpdate for each enabled addon every frame.

The Shroud* API surface is registered in InitAPICalls() and friends; per-frame globals
  (player position, health, time values) are pushed in SetGlobalVariables().

Callbacks run under an execution watchdog (commit 02261f6626): a callback that runs past
  its wall-clock budget (1 s for a normal callback, 5 s for load-time / ShroudOnStart) is
  aborted with a MoonSharpWatchdogException — which derives from System.Exception, not
  InterpreterException, so a pcall-wrapped infinite loop cannot swallow it. An addon that
  errors repeatedly (≥8 times in 10 s) is auto-disabled in memory until /lua reload. See the
  authoring guide's sandbox section for the player-facing summary.

Garbage collection API (#914)¶

MoonSharp has no Lua-side GC — Lua values are .NET objects collected by Unity's (Boehm) GC.
Stock MoonSharp mapped collectgarbage("collect") to a full blocking collect (measured
140-190ms on a live-sized heap) and returned nil for every other mode, so addons could neither
measure memory nor collect incrementally.

LuaGcApi (UnityProject/Assets/Scripts/Lua/LuaGcApi.cs) overrides collectgarbage in every
Script the host creates:

Call
Behavior
Returns

collectgarbage() / ("collect") / ("restart")
Full blocking collect (unchanged — still expensive, use "step" instead)
0

collectgarbage("count")
Managed heap size
KB, bytes % 1024 (two values, Lua 5.2 style)

collectgarbage("step"[, ms])
Time-budgeted incremental collect via GarbageCollector.CollectIncremental. Optional arg = millisecond budget (default 3, clamped 0.1-50). Lua's KB step arg has no CLR mapping. No-op returning true if incremental GC is unavailable — never falls back to a blocking collect.
true when the collection cycle is complete

collectgarbage("isrunning")
GC enabled check
boolean

any other mode ("stop", "setpause", "setstepmul", …)
No-op — addons cannot disable the client-wide GC
nil

The project ships with Unity incremental GC enabled (gcIncremental: 1), so automatic
collections are already time-sliced; "step" lets an addon voluntarily donate extra budget
(e.g. during loading screens) instead of forcing a stall with "collect".

Frame timing globals¶

ShroudDeltaTime — Time.deltaTime, clamped by the project's Maximum Allowed Timestep
  (0.1s, ProjectSettings/TimeManager.asset). During any stall longer than 100ms it saturates
  at ~0.1 — correct for pacing animation, wrong for measuring stalls. Kept clamped for
  back-compat.

ShroudRealDeltaTime (new, #914) — unclamped wall-clock frame delta
  (Time.realtimeSinceStartupAsDouble difference), shows the true length of long frames.
  Use this for addon-side hitch diagnostics.

Both are pushed once per frame after addon callbacks run, so a stall in frame N is visible to
addons one frame later.

Ink conversation variable bridge (#745)¶

Player-authored custom-NPC Ink scripts persist per-character state through their
saveVariable(varName)/loadVariable(varName) external functions
(UnityProject/Assets/Scripts/UIControllers/CustomNpc/CustomNpcStoryUI.cs), which read/write
local PlayerPrefs under the key <PhotonCharacterName>.Ink_<varName> (the character's full
name, "First" or "First Last"). LuaInkApi
(UnityProject/Assets/Scripts/Lua/LuaInkApi.cs) exposes the same key space to addons,
registered from InitAPICalls() with a character-name provider:

Call
Returns
Behavior

ShroudLoadInkVariable(varName)
string or nil
The stored string, or nil when unsaved / no character / bad varName. A saved "" returns "", not nil.

ShroudSaveInkVariable(varName, value)
boolean
Stores string / number / boolean; false (no write) for any other type, a string over 8192 chars, NaN/Inf, bad varName, or no character.

ShroudHasInkVariable(varName)
boolean
Whether a value is stored.

ShroudDeleteInkVariable(varName)
boolean
Removes the value; true only if one existed. Safe: Ink's loadVariable re-seeds the script default when the key is missing.

varName must be a non-empty Lua string (no coercion — a numeric 5 never aliases the key
...Ink_5). Value formatting matches what Ink's loadVariable int.TryParse round-trips:
integral numbers store without a decimal point (42 / 42.0 → "42"), non-integral store
invariant (3.5 → "3.5", which Ink reads back as a string), booleans store "1"/"0" (the
embedded Ink runtime has no bool type; int truthiness is its idiom).

Synchronization contract: the bridge only touches PlayerPrefs, never a running story's
in-memory variablesState. A conversation observes a Lua write at its next
loadVariable(var) call, and an addon observes a story write after the story's
saveVariable(var) — save/load are the explicit sync points, there are no notifications
(poll in ShroudOnUpdate if reacting matters).

Gotchas:

Ink's loadVariable treats the stored literal string "null" as "never saved" and resets
  the variable to the script default; the Lua side (HasKey-based) reads it back faithfully.
  Avoid storing "null" for values an Ink script must read.

Ink's loadVariable seeds the script's default into PlayerPrefs on first call, so
  ShroudHasInkVariable can be true for a variable a conversation merely loaded.

Keys are per character name and device-local (PlayerPrefs): renames orphan data,
  same-named characters on one machine share, other machines see nothing.

Writes are not flushed per call (parity with the Ink side; Unity flushes on clean quit).

Target API (#746)¶

Functions exposing the player's current target, for buff monitors and similar addons. The
target resolves exactly like the stock target frame: the locked (selected) target if there is
one, otherwise the closest/best target, and only combatants count. Implementations live in
LuaManager.cs (#region Target API); the pure decision logic (debuff mapping, hidden-health
clamp, stat policy) is in UnityProject/Assets/Scripts/Lua/LuaTargetLogic.cs so EditMode tests
can pin it.

Function
Returns
No target

ShroudHasTarget()
bool
false

ShroudGetTargetName()
string
"None"

ShroudGetTargetId()
int — session-local id, stable while the object lives; use it to detect target switches. Not persistent across sessions.
-1

ShroudIsTargetDead()
bool
false

ShroudIsTargetHealthHidden()
bool — true while the target hides its health (see below)
false

ShroudGetTargetCurrentHealth()
int
-1

ShroudGetTargetMaxHealth()
int
-1

ShroudGetTargetCurrentFocus() / ShroudGetTargetMaxFocus()
int
-1

ShroudGetTargetBuff()
List<RuneEffects> (same shape as ShroudGetPlayerBuff)
nil

ShroudGetTargetBuffCount()
int
0

ShroudGetTargetBuffName(i) / ShroudGetTargetBuffDescription(i)
string (0-based index)
"Invalid"

ShroudGetTargetBuffTimeRemaining(i)
float seconds
-1

ShroudGetTargetStatValueByNumber(n) / ShroudGetTargetStatValueByName(s)
float
InvalidStatResult

Behavior rules (all mirror what the stock UI already reveals — addons can never show more):

Hidden health: some creatures hide their health until they drop below half. While hidden,
  ShroudGetTargetCurrentHealth() reports the max value (exactly like the target frame's full
  bar) and ShroudIsTargetHealthHidden() returns true so an addon can render a "?" instead.

Player targets are vitals-only: when the target is another player, the stat functions
  return InvalidStatResult for everything except CurrentHealth, Health, CurrentFocus,
  and Focus. NPC/creature targets expose the full stat set minus the same hidden list the
  player stat functions use (virtues, GM/AI flags).

RuneEffects gained fields (also on ShroudGetPlayerBuff/ShroudGetPetBuff results):
  RuneId (int skill id), IsDebuff (bool, hostile-disposition runes), StackCount (number of
  grouped effect entries under the rune — a rune applying several effect components counts each
  one, so treat it as an upper bound on true stacks).

Feature detection: ShroudLuaApiVersion¶

Builds with the target API define the global ShroudLuaApiVersion (a plain number; bumped when
the API surface grows — 1 = target API #746, 2 = under-mouse API #1031). It is set at Script
creation, before addon files run, so reading it at addon top level is safe everywhere:

if ShroudLuaApiVersion and ShroudLuaApiVersion >= 1 then hasTargetApi = true end
if ShroudLuaApiVersion and ShroudLuaApiVersion >= 2 then hasUnderMouseApi = true end

Calling Shroud* functions at top level is still unsupported (they register after addon files
load); call them only inside callbacks like ShroudOnUpdate.

Perf notes¶

Every call resolves the target and every buff call snapshots the effect array (an allocation).
Prefer one ShroudGetTargetBuff() per ShroudOnUpdate over per-index Count/Name/Time
loops, and see collectgarbage("step") above for donating GC budget.

Under-mouse API (#1031)¶

Functions exposing whatever is under the mouse cursor — a world NPC or player, a world item or
container, a placed decoration, an inventory/vendor item, or a UI element with a tooltip. This is
the same "what is the cursor over" resolution the client runs every frame to build its own
tooltip (UIManager.ResolveTooltipUnderMouse): the world object first
(PlayerTargeting.TooltipObject / MouseTarget / HoveredDeco), then the NGUI element under the
cursor. The text-flattening and kind logic lives in
UnityProject/Assets/Scripts/Lua/LuaMouseLogic.cs so EditMode tests can pin it; the resolver and
bindings are in LuaManager.cs (#region Under-mouse API).

Function
Returns
Nothing under cursor

ShroudGetDescriptionUnderMouse()
string — the full tooltip text, markup stripped. Item tooltips come back as the name line, a newline, then the stat/description block.
""

ShroudGetNameUnderMouse()
string — the title line only (item name, interact text, scene/NPC name). Falls back to the entity's display name for live NPCs and players, which carry no tooltip.
""

ShroudGetKindUnderMouse()
string — "player", "npc", "item", "container", "deco", "object" (unclassified world object), or "ui".
"none"

ShroudGetIdUnderMouse()
int — session-local id of the world entity/deco, stable while it lives (same convention as ShroudGetTargetId); -1 for a pure UI hover.
-1

Behavior rules:

Ungated on purpose. Unlike the client's own tooltip, these functions ignore the display
  gating (mouse button held, HUD hidden, hover delay not yet elapsed), so an addon can read what
  the cursor is over at the exact moment of a click. The text is still only ever what the stock
  tooltip would show — addons never see more than the game already reveals.

Item kind travels with the item. An item tooltip reports kind "item" wherever it appears —
  world drop, inventory, container slot, vendor row, mail — not a generic "ui".

Per-frame cache. All four functions resolve once per frame (keyed on Time.frameCount);
  building an item tooltip formats a whole stat block, so calling all four in one ShroudOnUpdate
  costs one resolution, not four.

Known gaps. A skill tooltip reports the skill's name and description text, not the full
  computed stat panel the UI draws (that panel is built inside the tooltip prefab, not carried on
  the content). A handful of specialized tooltip types (plot-storage slot, skill-advancement mode)
  have no addon-readable text and return "" for the description while still reporting "ui".

Pair these with the existing ShroudMouseX / ShroudMouseY globals when an addon needs both the
screen position and the identity of what is under it.

Tests¶

UnityProject/Assets/Editor/PortedTests/LuaGcApiTests.cs (EditMode) pins the override's
contract, including the stock-MoonSharp nil-"count" precondition.
UnityProject/Assets/Editor/PortedTests/LuaInkApiTests.cs (EditMode) pins the Ink bridge:
the exact PlayerPrefs key format shared with CustomNpcStoryUI, value formatting, and the
fail-soft guards.

UnityProject/Assets/Editor/PortedTests/LuaTargetApiTests.cs pins the target API's pure logic:
debuff disposition mapping, the hidden-health clamp, the player-target vitals-only stat policy,
the legacy hidden-stat list, and the Lua-visible shape of the extended RuneEffects.

UnityProject/Assets/Editor/PortedTests/LuaMouseApiTests.cs pins the under-mouse API's pure
logic: how each TooltipContent type flattens into the description and name, markup stripping,
equipment-comparison using only the hovered item, and the kind precedence.
